questions.question: Does the company have a written Vision and Mission that the management team can state and that is used when taking major decisions?
questions.recommendation: Write a one-page Vision/Mission with the owner and department heads; display it and link every annual goal to it.
questions.business_risk: Decisions get taken case by case; departments pull in different directions and growth investments are inconsistent.

questions.question: Is there a documented 3-5 year business growth strategy covering products, customers, markets and capacity?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a 3-5 year growth strategy: target turnover, product lines, target customer segments, export/new markets and capacity/investment plan; review it every 6 months.
questions.business_risk: Growth stays opportunistic; capital is spent on whatever comes up and the company cannot explain to a bank, buyer or investor where it is going.

questions.question: Is an annual turnover (sales) target defined for the current financial year and broken down by month and by customer/product group?
questions.recommendation: Fix the annual turnover target, split it month-wise and customer/product-wise, and review actual vs target in the monthly management review.
questions.business_risk: Nobody knows in July that the year is being lost; shortfalls are discovered at year end when nothing can be done.

questions.question: Is an annual profitability target (EBITDA / PBT %) defined and tracked at least monthly?
questions.recommendation: Define EBITDA/PBT % target with the accountant; produce a monthly P&L within 10 days of month end and review margin vs target.
questions.business_risk: Turnover grows while profit erodes unnoticed; price and cost decisions are taken without knowing the margin impact.

questions.question: Is cash flow (collections, payments, working-capital limits) monitored at least weekly with a rolling forecast?
questions.recommendation: Introduce a weekly cash-flow statement and 8-week rolling forecast; review receivables ageing and payable commitments every Monday.
questions.business_risk: A profitable order book can still cause a liquidity crisis - delayed salaries, supplier stoppages and bank default risk.

questions.question: Are 1-year business goals defined for each department (sales, production, quality, purchase, HR) with owners and measurable targets?
questions.recommendation: Cascade the annual business plan into department goals with numeric targets, owners and monthly milestones; publish a one-page goal sheet.
questions.kpi: % of departments with approved annual goals
questions.business_risk: Department heads optimise their own area; company goals are not owned by anyone below the owner.

questions.question: Are 3-year growth targets (turnover, profit, capacity, customers) formally established and reviewed?
questions.recommendation: Set 3-year targets with yearly milestones for turnover, margin, capacity and customer count; review progress quarterly.
questions.business_risk: Investments in machines, land and people are made without a medium-term demand picture; over- or under-capacity results.

questions.question: Are new-customer acquisition targets (number and value) defined for the year?
questions.recommendation: Set a target for new customers by segment (e.g. 6 new customers, Rs X Cr), assign to sales/marketing and track monthly.
questions.kpi: New customers added vs target; new-customer revenue %
questions.business_risk: Business remains dependent on existing customers; any loss of one account directly hits turnover.

questions.question: Is customer concentration risk (share of top 1 and top 3 customers in turnover) measured and is there a plan to reduce it?
questions.recommendation: Calculate top-1 / top-3 customer share of sales; set a ceiling (e.g. no customer > 30%) and a diversification plan with target segments.
questions.business_risk: One customer's price cut, insourcing decision or slowdown can remove 40-60% of turnover overnight.

questions.question: Are export or new-market development targets defined with a specific plan (countries, certifications, channels)?
questions.recommendation: Identify 2-3 target export markets or new domestic segments; plan certifications, marketing channels and a yearly export revenue target.
questions.business_risk: Company stays exposed to one domestic market cycle and loses pricing power against export-ready competitors.

questions.question: Are new product / new process development targets defined with a review of development progress?
questions.recommendation: Set an NPD target (number of new parts/products per year) with stage-gate reviews; track development lead time and hit rate.
questions.kpi: New products launched vs target; NPD lead time
questions.business_risk: Product portfolio ages, margins compress and the company competes on price alone.

questions.question: Is future capacity requirement (machines, space, manpower) planned against the 3-year sales forecast?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a capacity vs demand chart for 3 years by process; decide expansion/outsourcing triggers and capex timing.
questions.kpi: Capacity utilisation %; capex plan vs actual
questions.business_risk: Orders are lost or delivered late because capacity is added only after a crisis, or capital is locked in idle machines.

questions.question: Are major business risks (customer loss, raw material price, key-person dependence, statutory, cyber) periodically identified and reviewed with mitigation plans?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a business risk register with likelihood/impact rating and mitigation owner; review it quarterly in the management review.
questions.kpi: Risk register reviewed (quarterly Y/N); high risks open
questions.business_risk: Foreseeable shocks - a key operator leaving, a steel price spike, a GST notice - arrive unplanned and are handled in panic.

questions.question: Is there a succession plan for the owner/MD and for key managers and key skilled positions?
questions.recommendation: Identify critical positions, name successors/second-line, and start structured development; document authority delegation.
questions.business_risk: The business cannot run without the owner; illness or an exit of one manager stops customers being served.

questions.question: Is business performance vs goals reviewed monthly by top management, with corrective actions recorded and followed up when targets are missed?
questions.recommendation: Hold a fixed monthly Management Review with a standard agenda (goals, KPIs, actions); record decisions and track closure of actions.
questions.kpi: Management review held (monthly Y/N); action closure %
questions.business_risk: Targets exist on paper only; missed targets are explained, not corrected, and the same problems repeat every year.

questions.question: Are department-wise KPIs formally defined in writing with formula, data source, frequency and owner?
questions.recommendation: Create a KPI Master: for each department define 3-6 KPIs with formula, data source, frequency, target and owner.
questions.kpi: No. of departments with defined KPIs
questions.business_risk: Everyone measures something different; management gets opinions instead of numbers.

questions.question: Does every KPI have a numeric target for the current year?
questions.recommendation: Set a target for every KPI based on last year's actual, customer requirement and business goals; approve in the management review.
questions.business_risk: Performance cannot be judged as good or bad; KPI reports become information, not a management tool.

questions.question: Are actual KPI values compared against targets every month with variance highlighted?
questions.recommendation: Produce a monthly KPI sheet showing target, actual, variance and trend with red/amber/green status.
questions.business_risk: Deviations are noticed only when a customer or auditor complains.

questions.question: Is a structured monthly management review held to discuss all KPIs, with minutes and action points?
questions.recommendation: Fix a monthly management review date; use a standard KPI deck; record actions with owner and date; review closure first in the next meeting.
questions.business_risk: Problems are discussed informally and forgotten; there is no organisational memory of decisions.

questions.question: Are corrective actions with owner and target date recorded when KPI targets are not achieved, and their closure tracked?
questions.recommendation: Introduce an action register linked to the KPI review; every red KPI must have a root-cause and an action; track closure %.
questions.business_risk: The same KPI stays red for months; reviews become blame sessions with no improvement.

questions.question: Is there a one-page management dashboard (MIS) that the owner/MD sees at least monthly?
questions.recommendation: Build a one-page owner dashboard with the 10 key business numbers (turnover, margin, cash, order book, RFQ pipeline, OTD, PPM, OEE, inventory days, productivity).
questions.business_risk: The owner runs the business on gut feel and on the loudest problem of the day.

questions.question: Is OEE (or at least machine utilisation and downtime) measured for critical machines?
questions.recommendation: Start daily OEE on bottleneck/critical machines: availability, performance, quality; review weekly with production and maintenance.
questions.business_risk: Hidden capacity losses of 20-30% remain invisible and new machines are bought instead of recovering existing capacity.

questions.question: Are internal rejection %, customer PPM and supplier PPM tracked monthly with targets?
questions.recommendation: Set up monthly rejection and PPM reporting by part/process/supplier with Pareto analysis and targets.
questions.kpi: Internal rejection %; Customer PPM; Supplier PPM
questions.business_risk: Quality cost stays hidden in scrap and rework; customer ratings drop before management notices.

questions.question: Is On-Time Delivery (OTD) to customers measured monthly by customer and by line?
questions.recommendation: Measure OTD (on-time-in-full) per customer monthly from despatch data vs schedule; analyse causes of misses.
questions.business_risk: Delivery failures erode customer ratings and lead to loss of new business allocation.

questions.question: Is productivity (output per man-hour or per machine-hour, or value added per employee) measured and reviewed?
questions.recommendation: Define productivity measures per line/process; publish monthly trend and set improvement targets.
questions.kpi: Output per man-hour; Value added per employee
questions.business_risk: Manpower cost grows faster than output; margins erode without anyone seeing where.

questions.question: Are inventory days / inventory turnover monitored monthly?
questions.recommendation: Calculate inventory days for RM, WIP and FG monthly; set targets and review slow-moving stock.
questions.business_risk: Working capital is locked in stock and the company borrows to fund it.

questions.question: Are receivables (debtor days, overdue %) monitored monthly with follow-up responsibility assigned?
questions.recommendation: Track debtor days and overdue ageing per customer weekly; assign collection responsibility and escalation rules.
questions.business_risk: Customers use the company as a bank; cash shortage despite good sales.

questions.question: Is product/customer-wise profitability (contribution margin) known and reviewed?
questions.recommendation: Prepare part-wise costing and contribution margin; review customer profitability quarterly and act on loss-making parts.
questions.business_risk: Loss-making parts are produced for years; volume growth reduces profit.

questions.question: Is employee productivity (turnover per employee, or value added per employee) tracked and benchmarked?
questions.recommendation: Track sales per employee and value added per employee monthly; compare with industry benchmarks and set targets.
questions.business_risk: Manpower additions are approved without knowing whether existing manpower is productive.

questions.question: Are KPI data captured from records/systems (not from memory) and validated before review?
questions.recommendation: Define data sources and formats for each KPI; assign data owners; cross-check KPI data with accounts and despatch records.
questions.business_risk: Decisions are taken on wrong numbers; reviews degenerate into arguments about data instead of actions.

questions.question: Is there an approved organisation chart with clear reporting lines, and is it up to date?
questions.recommendation: Prepare and approve an organisation chart with reporting lines and deputies; update it at every change.
questions.business_risk: Overlapping authority and unclear accountability - problems fall between departments.

questions.question: Is manpower requirement planned against the production plan (by skill, shift and section), including contract labour?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a manpower plan from the production plan: required vs available by skill and shift; plan recruitment/multi-skilling for gaps.
questions.business_risk: Production is lost for lack of skilled operators, or excess manpower is carried in low months.

questions.question: Do all staff and supervisory positions have written job descriptions with responsibilities and authority?
questions.recommendation: Write job descriptions (responsibility, authority, KPI, competency) for every position; sign off with the employee.
questions.business_risk: People do what they think their job is; critical tasks (e.g. calibration, PM) have no owner.

questions.question: Is there a defined recruitment process with selection criteria, and is time-to-hire tracked?
questions.recommendation: Define requisition, sourcing, interview and selection steps; track time-to-hire and quality of hire.
questions.business_risk: Positions remain vacant for months; wrong hires increase turnover and training cost.

questions.question: Do new employees (including contract workers) go through a structured induction covering safety, quality and job training before working independently?
questions.recommendation: Create an induction checklist: company, safety, quality policy, work instructions, on-job training and sign-off before release to line.
questions.business_risk: New operators cause rejections and accidents in their first weeks.

questions.question: Is there an annual training plan based on identified needs, and is its execution tracked?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a training need identification and annual calendar; track planned vs actual training and evaluate effectiveness.
questions.kpi: Training hours per employee; plan adherence %
questions.business_risk: Skills stay stagnant; new equipment and customer requirements are not absorbed.

questions.question: Is a skill matrix maintained for operators (level 1-4) for each critical operation?
questions.recommendation: Build a skill matrix for every critical operation; grade operators L1-L4; plan upgrades and use it for shift allocation.
questions.business_risk: One absentee stops a line; quality varies by shift because unskilled operators run critical processes.

questions.question: Is multi-skilling planned so that critical operations have at least 2-3 competent operators?
questions.recommendation: Plan multi-skilling from the skill matrix: target minimum 2 competent operators per critical operation; run cross-training monthly.
questions.business_risk: Dependence on individual operators; overtime and delays when they are absent.

questions.question: Is there an annual performance appraisal linked to KPIs/goals for staff, and is it used for increments and development?
questions.recommendation: Introduce a KPI-linked appraisal for staff; hold mid-year and annual reviews; link increments and training to the outcome.
questions.business_risk: High performers leave for lack of recognition; poor performers stay for lack of evidence.

questions.question: Is employee turnover (attrition %) measured monthly with exit reasons analysed and actions taken?
questions.recommendation: Track attrition monthly by category; conduct exit interviews; analyse reasons and act on the top causes.
questions.business_risk: Constant re-hiring and re-training; quality and productivity suffer from inexperience.

questions.question: Are attendance and absenteeism tracked daily and reviewed with actions (shift planning, discipline, incentives)?
questions.recommendation: Use a biometric/attendance register; publish daily absenteeism %; plan shifts with buffer and act on chronic absentees.
questions.business_risk: Daily production plans fail for want of people; overtime cost rises.

questions.question: Is employee productivity measured and linked to an incentive or recognition scheme?
questions.recommendation: Define productivity measures per section; introduce a transparent incentive/recognition scheme linked to output, quality and attendance.
questions.kpi: Output per man-hour; incentive payout vs productivity gain
questions.business_risk: No reason for employees to improve; good and poor performers are paid the same.

questions.question: Are HR statutory compliances (PF, ESIC, Factories Act, contract labour, minimum wages) tracked with a compliance calendar?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a statutory compliance calendar with owner and evidence; audit quarterly; ensure contractor compliance.
questions.business_risk: Penalties, prosecution and customer audit failures; loss of approved-supplier status.

questions.question: Are supervisors and second-line managers developed through training and delegated responsibility?
questions.recommendation: Identify second-line leaders; give them KPI ownership, structured training and regular coaching from the owner/GM.
questions.business_risk: The owner remains the only decision-maker; growth is limited by the owner's time.

questions.question: Are regular employee communication meetings (daily line meeting, monthly all-hands) held and are employee suggestions collected and implemented?
questions.recommendation: Start a 10-minute daily line meeting and a monthly communication meeting; run a suggestion scheme with recognition.
questions.kpi: Suggestions implemented per employee per year
questions.business_risk: Low ownership on the shop floor; problems known to operators never reach management.

questions.question: Is there a written marketing strategy defining how the company will win new business over the next 1-3 years?
questions.recommendation: Write a marketing plan: target segments, value proposition, channels (digital, exhibitions, referrals), budget and monthly lead targets.
questions.kpi: Marketing plan approved (Y/N); leads per month
questions.business_risk: New business depends on chance enquiries and the owner's personal contacts.

questions.question: Are target industries and target customer profile (ideal customer: size, product, location) clearly defined?
questions.recommendation: Define 2-3 target industries and an Ideal Customer Profile (turnover, products bought, volumes, location); focus all marketing on it.
questions.business_risk: Effort is spread across every enquiry; quotations are prepared for customers that will never convert.

questions.question: Is a named list of target customers (prospects) maintained with status of approach?
questions.recommendation: Build a prospect list of 50-100 named companies with contact, status and next action; review it monthly.
questions.business_risk: Marketing activity cannot be measured; no pipeline of future customers.

questions.question: Is competitor information (products, prices, customers, capacities) collected and reviewed at least yearly?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a competitor comparison sheet for the top 5 competitors; update annually and use it in pricing and positioning.
questions.business_risk: Pricing and capability decisions are made blind; the company discovers competitors only when it loses an order.

questions.question: Does the company have a professional, up-to-date website that shows products, processes, machines, certifications and customers, with an enquiry form?
questions.recommendation: Upgrade the website: product/process pages, plant and machine list, certifications, customer logos, enquiry form; keep it updated quarterly.
questions.business_risk: Buyers checking the company online see nothing credible and move to a competitor.

questions.question: Is LinkedIn (company page and owner profile) actively used with regular posts to reach buyers and purchase managers?
questions.recommendation: Optimise the company page and key profiles; post 2-4 times a month (capabilities, deliveries, certifications); connect with buyers in target industries.
questions.business_risk: The company is invisible to the purchase managers who now source suppliers online.

questions.question: Is digital marketing (Google Business, B2B portals like IndiaMART/TradeIndia, SEO, ads) used and its results measured?
questions.recommendation: Set up Google Business profile, B2B portal listings and basic SEO; track enquiries by source monthly and invest where leads convert.
questions.kpi: Leads per channel per month; cost per lead
questions.business_risk: Competitors with online presence capture the enquiries; the company depends on walk-ins and references.

questions.question: Is there a systematic B2B lead-generation process (cold outreach, exhibitions, referrals, portals) with a monthly lead target?
questions.recommendation: Define a lead generation system: sources, monthly lead target, responsible person, follow-up steps and a lead register.
questions.business_risk: New enquiries are random; sales growth cannot be planned.

questions.question: Are export marketing activities (buyer databases, international portals, exhibitions, certifications) planned and executed?
questions.recommendation: Identify export target markets and buyer databases; list on international portals; plan one international exhibition/buyer-seller meet per year.
questions.business_risk: Export remains an aspiration; foreign buyers cannot find or qualify the company.

questions.question: Is a complete customer and prospect database (contacts, decision makers, products, potential) maintained and updated?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a CRM or Excel database of customers and prospects with decision makers, products, potential value and last contact.
questions.kpi: Database records updated in last 90 days %
questions.business_risk: Customer knowledge sits in individuals' phones and leaves with them.

questions.question: Does the company have a consistent brand identity and professional collateral (company profile, brochure, presentation, machine list)?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a company profile, capability presentation and brochure with consistent branding; update yearly.
questions.business_risk: The company looks like a job-shop even when it has strong capability; it loses on perception.

questions.question: Are customer visits, exhibitions and buyer meets planned with a yearly calendar and budget?
questions.recommendation: Plan a yearly calendar of customer visits, exhibitions and industry events with budget and expected leads; review results.
questions.kpi: Exhibitions/visits done vs plan; leads generated
questions.business_risk: Relationships with buyers weaken; competitors are more visible at the customer.

questions.question: Are marketing KPIs (enquiries per month, lead source, conversion, cost per lead) defined and reviewed monthly?
questions.recommendation: Define marketing KPIs and review them monthly alongside sales KPIs; adjust channel spend based on conversion.
questions.business_risk: Marketing spend cannot be justified or optimised; it is cut first when cash is tight.

questions.question: Is the return on marketing spend (business won vs spend by channel) evaluated?
questions.recommendation: Track marketing spend by channel and revenue from customers acquired through each channel; calculate yearly ROI.
questions.business_risk: Money is spent on channels that do not produce customers.

questions.question: Are certifications required by target customers (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, CE, etc.) obtained or planned?
questions.recommendation: Identify certifications demanded by target customers/markets; plan implementation with timeline and budget.
questions.kpi: Certifications held vs required by target customers
questions.business_risk: The company is disqualified from RFQs before it can quote.

questions.question: Is a sales target defined for the year and broken down by month, customer and product group, with a named owner?
questions.recommendation: Set monthly sales targets by customer and product group; assign owners; review actual vs target weekly.
questions.business_risk: Sales are whatever customers schedule; the company cannot plan production, purchase or cash.

questions.question: Is a sales pipeline (enquiries -> RFQ -> quotation -> negotiation -> order) maintained with value and stage?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a pipeline register with stage, value, probability and next action; review weekly.
questions.business_risk: Future sales are unknown; a dry pipeline is noticed only when orders stop.

questions.question: Are all RFQs/enquiries logged with date, customer, part, value, and status, and is RFQ conversion % measured?
questions.recommendation: Log every RFQ in an RFQ register; measure RFQs received, quoted, won and conversion % monthly; analyse losses.
questions.business_risk: Enquiries are lost or quoted late; the company never learns why it loses.

questions.question: Is there a standard quotation process with costing sheet, approval authority and response-time target (e.g. 3-5 days)?
questions.recommendation: Standardise quotation: costing sheet, margin check, approval authority, quotation format and 3-5 day turnaround; track quotation lead time.
questions.business_risk: Slow or inconsistent quotes lose orders; under-priced quotes lose money for years.

questions.question: Is there a disciplined follow-up system for open quotations and enquiries with dates and responsibility?
questions.recommendation: Assign follow-up dates for every open quotation; review weekly; record customer feedback and reasons for loss.
questions.kpi: Open quotations followed up on time %
questions.business_risk: Quotations die silently; competitors who follow up win.

questions.question: Is there a plan and target for acquiring new customers, with a defined approach to each target account?
questions.recommendation: Set new-customer targets by segment; prepare an account plan per target; track approach status monthly.
questions.kpi: New customers won per year; new-customer sales %
questions.business_risk: Growth depends on existing customers giving more volume.

questions.question: Is customer retention monitored (customers lost, business lost, share of business at each customer)?
questions.recommendation: Track share of business at each key customer and lost business; hold quarterly review meetings with key customers.
questions.business_risk: Customers drift to competitors without any warning signal reaching management.

questions.question: Is a rolling 3-6 month sales forecast prepared from customer schedules and shared with production and purchase?
questions.recommendation: Collect customer schedules/forecasts monthly; prepare a 3-6 month rolling forecast and use it for capacity, manpower and material planning.
questions.business_risk: Production and purchase react to weekly schedules; expediting cost, stock-outs and overtime result.

questions.question: Is customer interaction (visits, calls, complaints, commitments) recorded in a CRM or a structured register?
questions.recommendation: Implement a simple CRM (or structured Excel) for contacts, interactions, commitments and follow-ups.
questions.kpi: CRM entries per week; commitments closed on time %
questions.business_risk: Commitments to customers are forgotten; relationship knowledge leaves with sales staff.

questions.question: Is the confirmed order book (value and months of cover) known at any time and reviewed monthly?
questions.recommendation: Maintain an order book register; report order book value and months of cover monthly to the owner.
questions.kpi: Order book value; months of cover
questions.business_risk: The company cannot see a downturn coming or plan capacity for an upturn.

questions.question: Is pricing based on a costing sheet with target margin, and are prices reviewed when raw material or other costs change?
questions.recommendation: Use a standard costing sheet for every quotation; define target margin by product group; review prices on RM/ conversion cost changes with a price-revision process.
questions.kpi: Price revisions realised vs cost increase %
questions.business_risk: Cost increases are absorbed; margin disappears while turnover grows.

questions.question: Is the contribution margin known part-wise and customer-wise, and is it used in accepting orders?
questions.recommendation: Calculate contribution margin per part and per customer; set minimum acceptable margin; review loss-making parts for price correction or exit.
questions.business_risk: Low-margin parts consume capacity that could serve profitable business.

questions.question: Is profitability by customer reviewed at least quarterly and used to decide where to grow?
questions.recommendation: Prepare customer-wise P&L (sales, material, conversion, logistics, payment terms); decide grow/maintain/exit strategy per customer.
questions.business_risk: Effort is spent on large but unprofitable customers.

questions.question: Are receivables followed up systematically by sales/accounts against agreed credit terms, with escalation for overdues?
questions.recommendation: Define credit terms per customer; weekly overdue review; escalation matrix; link sales incentives to collections.
questions.business_risk: Cash is locked in receivables; the company borrows to fund customers.

questions.question: Are sales KPIs (target achievement, RFQ conversion, new customers, order book, receivables) reviewed monthly with actions?
questions.recommendation: Review sales KPIs in the monthly management review with actions and owners.
questions.business_risk: Sales performance is judged by feel; problems are noticed late.

questions.question: Is there a defined process for selecting new suppliers (capability assessment, samples, commercial terms) before approval?
questions.recommendation: Define supplier selection criteria and an assessment checklist; approve suppliers only after capability check and sample approval.
questions.business_risk: Wrong suppliers cause quality and delivery failures that surface at the customer.

questions.question: Is an Approved Supplier List (ASL) maintained by commodity and are purchases made only from approved suppliers?
questions.recommendation: Create an ASL by material/service category with approval status and scope; purchase only from ASL suppliers.
questions.business_risk: Uncontrolled sourcing; traceability and quality cannot be assured to customers.

questions.question: Are suppliers evaluated periodically (at least yearly) for quality, delivery, cost and service?
questions.recommendation: Implement a supplier scorecard (Quality, Cost, Delivery, Responsiveness); evaluate quarterly/yearly; communicate results to suppliers.
questions.business_risk: Poor suppliers continue for years; good suppliers are not rewarded.

questions.question: Is supplier rating (A/B/C) communicated to suppliers with improvement expectations?
questions.recommendation: Share rating and scorecard with suppliers; agree improvement actions for B/C suppliers; review in supplier meets.
questions.business_risk: Suppliers do not know what the company expects; improvement never happens.

questions.question: Is there a supplier development plan for critical suppliers (audits, training, process improvement)?
questions.recommendation: Identify critical suppliers; plan development actions (audits, training, joint improvement projects) and track results.
questions.kpi: Development actions closed; critical supplier PPM trend
questions.business_risk: Supplier problems are managed by inspection and rejection instead of prevention.

questions.question: Are critical suppliers audited periodically (process audit / system audit) with corrective actions tracked?
questions.recommendation: Prepare an annual supplier audit plan for critical suppliers; use a standard checklist; track corrective action closure.
questions.kpi: Supplier audits done vs plan; CA closure %
questions.business_risk: Process changes at suppliers go unnoticed until parts fail.

questions.question: Is supplier PPM / incoming rejection measured supplier-wise monthly?
questions.recommendation: Record incoming inspection results per supplier; calculate PPM monthly; act on the top 3 suppliers.
questions.business_risk: Supplier defects consume inspection, rework and line time and escape to the customer.

questions.question: Is supplier on-time delivery measured monthly?
questions.recommendation: Record promised vs actual delivery date per PO; calculate supplier OTD monthly; escalate poor performers.
questions.business_risk: Material shortages stop production; expediting and premium freight costs rise.

questions.question: Is there an annual purchase cost-reduction target with tracked projects (negotiation, alternate materials, VA/VE, consolidation)?
questions.recommendation: Set an annual purchase cost saving target (e.g. 2-3%); run projects; track savings monthly.
questions.business_risk: Material cost (often 50-65% of sales) drifts upward and profit erodes.

questions.question: Are alternate/second suppliers developed for critical materials and single-source items?
questions.recommendation: List single-source items; develop and approve alternates for critical ones; keep approved alternate samples ready.
questions.business_risk: One supplier's failure, strike or price demand stops production.

questions.question: Is raw material availability planned against the production plan with safety stock for critical items?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a material requirement plan from the production plan; define safety stock and lead times for critical items; review shortages daily.
questions.business_risk: Machines and manpower wait for material; delivery commitments are missed.

questions.question: Is purchasing done against a plan/MRP (not only urgent indents), with lead times and economic order quantities considered?
questions.recommendation: Introduce monthly purchase planning from the production plan and stock levels; fix reorder levels and lead times per item.
questions.business_risk: Emergency purchases at premium price and quality risk become normal.

questions.question: Are raw material price trends (steel, aluminium, polymers, etc.) tracked and used in purchasing and customer price revision?
questions.recommendation: Track commodity index prices monthly; use them for purchase timing and to trigger customer price-revision requests.
questions.business_risk: Price increases are absorbed by the company while customers are not informed in time.

questions.question: Are supplier risks (financial health, single source, location, capacity) assessed and mitigated?
questions.recommendation: Assess critical suppliers for financial, capacity and location risk annually; keep mitigation plans (alternate source, buffer stock).
questions.business_risk: A supplier closure or disaster causes an unplanned production stoppage.

questions.question: Are purchase KPIs (supplier PPM, OTD, cost saving, inventory, emergency purchases) reviewed monthly?
questions.recommendation: Include purchase KPIs in the monthly management review with actions.
questions.business_risk: Purchase performance is judged only by price; total cost of poor supply is invisible.

questions.question: Is a monthly/weekly production plan prepared from customer schedules and forecasts, and shared with all departments?
questions.recommendation: Prepare a monthly plan from customer schedules and a weekly/daily schedule per machine; publish to production, purchase, quality and maintenance.
questions.business_risk: Production runs on urgent calls from despatch; changeovers, shortages and overtime multiply.

questions.question: Is capacity (machine hours available vs required) calculated by process/machine and used to accept orders and plan shifts?
questions.recommendation: Calculate available vs required hours by machine/process monthly; identify bottlenecks; decide shifts, outsourcing or capex.
questions.business_risk: Orders are accepted beyond capacity or capacity lies idle; delivery promises are unreliable.

questions.question: Is a daily machine-wise schedule issued and is actual vs plan reviewed daily (daily production meeting)?
questions.recommendation: Issue a daily machine-wise schedule; hold a 15-minute daily production meeting on plan vs actual, losses and today's priorities.
questions.business_risk: Supervisors decide what to run; priority parts get delayed.

questions.question: Is production achievement % (actual vs plan) measured daily and monthly with reasons for shortfall?
questions.recommendation: Record actual vs plan per shift/machine with loss reasons; publish daily and monthly achievement % with Pareto of losses.
questions.business_risk: Shortfalls are found at month end when the customer schedule is already missed.

questions.question: Is productivity (pieces per man-hour / machine-hour) measured per line and compared with standard?
questions.recommendation: Set standard output per machine/operation; measure actual productivity per shift; review variance and improve.
questions.business_risk: Costs are estimated on assumed output that is never achieved; quotes lose money.

questions.question: Is OEE measured on critical/bottleneck machines with availability, performance and quality losses analysed?
questions.recommendation: Implement OEE on bottleneck machines: record downtime, speed loss and rejections per shift; review weekly; target improvement.
questions.business_risk: Hidden losses of 25-40% remain; capacity is bought instead of recovered.

questions.question: Is machine utilisation (running hours vs available hours) tracked machine-wise?
questions.recommendation: Log machine running hours vs available hours; identify low-utilisation machines and reasons; plan loading or disposal.
questions.business_risk: Investment in machines yields poor return; idle machines still cost depreciation and space.

questions.question: Are standard cycle times defined for every operation and compared with actual?
questions.recommendation: Establish standard cycle times through time study; record actual cycle time; act on variance >10%.
questions.business_risk: Capacity, costing and delivery planning rest on guesses.

questions.question: Are bottleneck operations identified and is the line balanced or the bottleneck de-bottlenecked?
questions.recommendation: Map process flow with cycle times; identify the constraint; balance or add capacity at the bottleneck; protect it from downtime.
questions.business_risk: Whole plant output is limited by one operation while others wait.

questions.question: Is machine downtime recorded by reason (breakdown, setup, material, manpower, quality) and analysed?
questions.recommendation: Record downtime per machine per shift with reason codes; Pareto monthly; assign actions to maintenance/production/stores.
questions.business_risk: The same losses recur daily and nobody owns them.

questions.question: Are setup/changeover times measured and reduced (SMED) for key machines?
questions.recommendation: Measure setup times; apply SMED (external vs internal setup, standard tooling, checklists); target 30-50% reduction.
questions.business_risk: Large batch sizes, high inventory and poor flexibility to customer schedule changes.

questions.question: Is in-process rejection % measured operation-wise daily with root-cause actions?
questions.recommendation: Record rejections per operation with defect codes; daily review of top defects; corrective actions with owners.
questions.business_risk: Scrap and rework cost 3-8% of sales unnoticed; customer PPM follows.

questions.question: Is rework quantity and cost tracked separately and reduced?
questions.recommendation: Record rework separately from rejection; cost it (labour + machine); analyse causes; set reduction target.
questions.business_risk: Rework hides process problems and consumes capacity that looks like production.

questions.question: Are work instructions / operation standards available at every workstation and followed?
questions.recommendation: Prepare visual work instructions with parameters, checks and safety points at each station; audit adherence weekly.
questions.business_risk: Quality depends on the operator; every shift produces differently.

questions.question: Is 5S / visual management practised with regular audits and display of daily performance boards?
questions.recommendation: Implement 5S with zone owners and monthly audits; put up daily performance boards (plan/actual/rejection/downtime) at each line.
questions.business_risk: Time is lost searching; problems are invisible; customer audits score poorly.

questions.question: Is incoming material inspected against defined specifications with records, and are results used for supplier rating?
questions.recommendation: Define incoming inspection plan (parameters, sampling, instruments) per item; record results; feed supplier PPM.
questions.business_risk: Defective material enters production and is discovered at final inspection or at the customer.

questions.question: Is in-process inspection (first-piece, patrol, last-piece) carried out as per control plan with records?
questions.recommendation: Define in-process checks per operation (frequency, instrument, reaction plan); record results; react on out-of-spec immediately.
questions.business_risk: Whole batches are produced defective before the problem is caught.

questions.question: Is final inspection / pre-despatch inspection done as per customer requirements with released records?
questions.recommendation: Define PDI checklist per customer/part; record and release lots only after PDI approval; retain records.
questions.business_risk: Defects reach the customer; line rejections, debit notes and rating loss follow.

questions.question: Are PFMEAs prepared for all processes, and updated after failures or customer complaints?
questions.recommendation: Prepare PFMEA for each process family; identify high RPN items and add controls; update after complaints or changes.
questions.kpi: PFMEA coverage %; high RPN items open
questions.business_risk: Known failure modes are not controlled; the same defects recur.

questions.question: Are control plans available for all parts/processes and consistent with PFMEA and inspection records?
questions.recommendation: Prepare control plans per part/process family linking characteristics, specs, methods and reaction plans; align with PFMEA and WIs.
questions.business_risk: Inspectors check what they think matters; critical characteristics may be uncontrolled.

questions.question: Is SPC applied to critical characteristics with Cp/Cpk monitored and actions taken when capability is low?
questions.recommendation: Identify critical characteristics; run X-bar/R or capability studies; act when Cpk < 1.33.
questions.business_risk: Process variation is unknown; parts drift towards rejection without warning.

questions.question: Are measurement systems (gauges, instruments, inspectors) validated through MSA/GR&R for critical characteristics?
questions.recommendation: Conduct GR&R studies on critical gauges annually; act when GR&R > 10-30%.
questions.business_risk: Good parts are rejected and bad parts accepted because of measurement error.

questions.question: Are all measuring instruments and gauges calibrated on schedule with traceable certificates and status labels?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a calibration register with frequency, due dates and status labels; use NABL-traceable labs; recall overdue instruments.
questions.business_risk: Measurement results cannot be trusted; customer audits fail; wrong parts are shipped as good.

questions.question: Are non-conformances recorded, segregated, and disposed through a defined process (rework, reject, use-as-is with approval)?
questions.recommendation: Introduce an NCR register and red-tag/segregation area; define disposition authority; analyse NCR trends monthly.
questions.business_risk: Rejected parts get mixed with good parts; non-conforming products are shipped.

questions.question: Are customer complaints logged, responded within the agreed time and analysed for recurrence?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a complaint register with response time and closure; respond with containment in 24 hours; review recurrence monthly.
questions.kpi: Customer complaints per month; response time
questions.business_risk: Customers escalate to new-business holds; the company's rating and future allocation drop.

questions.question: Is structured problem-solving (8D / Why-Why / fishbone) used for customer complaints and major internal failures, with effectiveness verified?
questions.recommendation: Train a core team in 8D; use it for every customer complaint and major failure; verify effectiveness after 3 months.
questions.business_risk: Repeat complaints for the same defect; corrective action is a paper exercise.

questions.question: Are internal quality system and process audits (layered / product audits) conducted as per plan with corrective actions closed?
questions.recommendation: Prepare an annual internal audit plan (system, process, product); train auditors; track NC closure.
questions.business_risk: The system exists only for certification audits; actual practice drifts.

questions.question: Is supplier quality managed through incoming data, supplier corrective action requests and supplier audits?
questions.recommendation: Issue SCARs for supplier defects; track supplier 8D closure; audit critical suppliers annually.
questions.business_risk: Supplier defects are absorbed by inspection and rework at the company's cost.

questions.question: Is Cost of Poor Quality (scrap, rework, sorting, warranty, debit notes, premium freight) calculated monthly as % of sales?
questions.recommendation: Compile COPQ monthly from scrap, rework, sorting, complaints, debit notes and premium freight; review as % of sales; target reduction.
questions.business_risk: Management sees quality as a cost centre because the far larger cost of poor quality is invisible.

questions.question: Are quality KPIs (customer PPM, internal rejection, COPQ, complaints, first pass yield) reviewed monthly with actions?
questions.recommendation: Review quality KPIs in the monthly management review; assign actions; track trends.
questions.business_risk: Quality performance drifts; problems are discovered by customers.

questions.question: Is a preventive maintenance schedule implemented for all machines with checklists, frequency and adherence tracking?
questions.recommendation: Establish a preventive maintenance schedule for all machines (priority to critical): frequency, checklist, responsibility; track PM adherence %.
questions.business_risk: Breakdowns dominate; machine life shortens; deliveries and quality suffer.

questions.question: Is predictive/condition-based maintenance (vibration, thermography, oil analysis) used for critical machines?
questions.recommendation: Start basic condition monitoring (vibration, temperature, oil) on critical machines; set alarm limits and act before failure.
questions.business_risk: Sudden failures of critical machines cause long, expensive stoppages.

questions.question: Are all breakdowns recorded with machine, time, duration, cause and repair action?
questions.recommendation: Maintain a breakdown register (start, end, cause code, action, spares used); analyse monthly.
questions.business_risk: The same failures recur because no one knows the pattern.

questions.question: Is maintenance work planned and scheduled in coordination with production (planned shutdown windows)?
questions.recommendation: Agree weekly maintenance windows with production; plan PM and pending jobs; publish a weekly maintenance plan.
questions.kpi: Planned vs unplanned maintenance hours ratio
questions.business_risk: Maintenance always fights production for machine time; PM is skipped.

questions.question: Is a machine history card/file maintained for every machine (breakdowns, PM, spares, modifications)?
questions.recommendation: Create a history record per machine; update with every breakdown, PM and spare change; use it for replacement decisions.
questions.business_risk: Repair decisions are made blind; chronic machines are not identified.

questions.question: Are critical machines identified (bottleneck, single machine, safety, high repair cost) with a higher maintenance priority?
questions.recommendation: Classify machines A/B/C by criticality; give A machines higher PM frequency, spares and condition monitoring.
questions.business_risk: Maintenance effort is spread evenly; the machine that stops the plant gets no special attention.

questions.question: Are critical spares identified, stocked at defined minimum levels and tracked?
questions.recommendation: List critical spares per A/B machine; define min/max; track consumption; establish suppliers with lead times.
questions.business_risk: A Rs 5,000 spare stops a Rs 50 lakh machine for a week.

questions.question: Is MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) calculated for critical machines and trended?
questions.recommendation: Calculate MTBF = operating hours / number of failures per machine monthly; trend and target improvement.
questions.business_risk: Reliability improvement cannot be measured or targeted.

questions.question: Is MTTR (Mean Time To Repair) calculated and reduced through spares, skills and standard repair procedures?
questions.recommendation: Calculate MTTR = total repair time / number of failures; reduce with spares availability, repair SOPs and skill training.
questions.business_risk: Every breakdown takes longer than necessary; production loss compounds.

questions.question: Is machine availability (%) tracked for critical machines against a target?
questions.recommendation: Calculate availability = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR) or running/planned time per critical machine monthly; set targets.
questions.business_risk: Capacity and delivery planning assume availability that the plant does not deliver.

questions.question: Are breakdowns analysed (Pareto, why-why) monthly and permanent countermeasures implemented?
questions.recommendation: Hold a monthly breakdown analysis: top machines/causes; root-cause; countermeasures; verify recurrence.
questions.business_risk: Maintenance remains firefighting; costs and downtime never come down.

questions.question: Do operators perform daily cleaning, inspection and lubrication (autonomous maintenance) with checklists?
questions.recommendation: Introduce daily operator checklists (clean-inspect-lubricate-tighten); train operators; audit weekly.
questions.business_risk: Minor abnormalities become major breakdowns; maintenance staff are overloaded.

questions.question: Is maintenance cost (spares, labour, contractors) tracked machine-wise and reviewed?
questions.recommendation: Track maintenance cost per machine monthly; review high-cost machines for overhaul/replacement.
questions.business_risk: Money is poured into chronic machines that should be replaced.

questions.question: Are utilities (power, compressed air, water) monitored for consumption and losses (leakages, power factor) with reduction actions?
questions.recommendation: Meter major consumers; track units per unit of output; fix air leaks and power factor; set a reduction target.
questions.business_risk: Energy cost (often 5-10% of sales) rises unnoticed.

questions.question: Are maintenance KPIs (breakdown hours, PM adherence, MTBF, MTTR, cost) reviewed monthly with actions?
questions.recommendation: Review maintenance KPIs in the monthly management review with actions and owners.
questions.business_risk: Maintenance is noticed only when the plant stops.

questions.question: Is raw material stock controlled with defined min/max or reorder levels and daily stock statements?
questions.recommendation: Define min/max/reorder levels per RM item from consumption and lead time; publish daily stock status; act on below-minimum items.
questions.kpi: RM stock-outs per month; RM inventory days
questions.business_risk: Either production stops for material or cash is locked in excess stock - often both.

questions.question: Is work-in-process inventory monitored (quantity, value, location) and controlled through planning?
questions.recommendation: Track WIP by stage weekly; set WIP limits per stage; reduce through flow and batch-size control.
questions.business_risk: Weeks of unfinished parts hide problems and lock working capital.

questions.question: Is finished goods stock controlled against customer schedules (days of cover) and despatch plan?
questions.recommendation: Set FG target days of cover per customer; review FG ageing weekly; produce to schedule, not to stock.
questions.business_risk: Over-production for one customer, shortage for another; obsolete FG when drawings change.

questions.question: Is FIFO (first-in-first-out) practised and traceable for raw material, WIP and finished goods?
questions.recommendation: Implement FIFO through location layout, date/batch tagging and issue rules; audit monthly.
questions.business_risk: Aged and mixed lots cause quality failures and loss of traceability at the customer.

questions.question: Is ABC (value-based) classification used to focus control on high-value items?
questions.recommendation: Classify items by annual consumption value; apply tighter control, counting and review to A items.
questions.business_risk: Equal effort on Rs 10 items and Rs 10 lakh items; high-value stock is poorly controlled.

questions.question: Are safety stock levels defined for critical items based on lead time and consumption variability?
questions.recommendation: Calculate safety stock for critical/long-lead items; review quarterly; do not hold safety stock on non-critical items.
questions.business_risk: Stock-outs of critical items or blanket buffers on everything.

questions.question: Is a reorder/indent system in place that triggers purchase automatically when stock reaches reorder level?
questions.recommendation: Set reorder levels and quantities per item; generate purchase indents from stock status, not from memory.
questions.business_risk: Purchase learns of shortages from production; premium-cost emergency buying.

questions.question: Is stock record accuracy measured (physical vs book) and maintained above 95%?
questions.recommendation: Measure stock accuracy through cycle counts; investigate variances; fix root causes (issue discipline, location, data entry).
questions.business_risk: Planning and purchasing on wrong stock data - shortages and excess simultaneously.

questions.question: Is perpetual/cycle counting done (A items monthly, B quarterly, C half-yearly) instead of relying only on year-end stock taking?
questions.recommendation: Implement a cycle-count calendar by ABC class; record variances and corrections.
questions.business_risk: Year-end stock shocks; audit qualifications; unknown losses.

questions.question: Is slow-moving inventory (no movement in 90/180 days) identified monthly and actioned?
questions.recommendation: Report slow-moving items monthly (>90/180 days); decide use/sell/return/scrap with owner approval.
questions.business_risk: Working capital slowly converts into unusable stock.

questions.question: Is dead/obsolete stock identified, valued and disposed with management approval?
questions.recommendation: Identify obsolete items (drawing changes, discontinued parts); value and dispose; prevent recurrence through ECN control.
questions.business_risk: Balance sheet shows inventory value that does not exist as usable material.

questions.question: Is an inventory ageing report (0-30, 31-90, 91-180, >180 days) prepared and reviewed monthly?
questions.recommendation: Produce a monthly ageing report by category; review in management review; act on >90-day stock.
questions.business_risk: Ageing stock is discovered only when it becomes unusable.

questions.question: Is physical stock verification done at defined frequency with reconciliation and approval of adjustments?
questions.recommendation: Schedule physical verification (quarterly/half-yearly); reconcile variances; approve adjustments at management level.
questions.business_risk: Losses, pilferage and record errors go undetected for a year.

questions.question: Are inventory days and inventory turnover calculated monthly with targets for RM, WIP and FG?
questions.recommendation: Calculate inventory days (stock value / daily consumption) for RM, WIP, FG monthly; set targets; review actions.
questions.business_risk: Working capital need grows faster than sales; bank limits are exhausted.

questions.question: Are stores organised with identified locations, controlled issue/receipt documentation and restricted access?
questions.recommendation: Organise stores with location codes, bin cards/system, controlled issue slips and restricted access; apply 5S.
questions.business_risk: Material is lost, mixed or issued without record; stock data is unreliable.
